newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta sees snow, frost, east Prairies frost free.
newsitem.headline: Alberta sees snow, frost, east Prairies frost free.

text.p: South and central Alberta's grainbelt saw a general frost Monday morning but Saskatchewan and Manitoba were frost free, Environment Canada said.

Calgary saw snow and an overnight low of -2.0 Celsius for most of the night. Central Alberta, between Calgary and Edmonton, saw an overnight low of -4.0 Celsius for most of the night, meteorologist Phil Wright said.
"It was pretty cool in Alberta, there was a general frost in south and central Alberta but not much frost in the extreme south or the far north of Alberta," Wright said.
Fifty percent of harvest was complete in central Alberta.
Lethbridge saw an overnight low of 0 Celsius (32 F) as did Edmonton, he said.
Saskatchewan and Manitoba did not see any overnight frost, he said.
Alberta should see a mix of sun and cloud with some rain and highs of 9.0 to 11 Celsius.
Saskatchewan should see partly cloudy skies and rain with highs of 10 to 16 Celsius.
Manitoba should see mainly cloudy skies, scattered showers and highs of 12 to 16 Celsius.
